newsitem.title: INDIA: Former Rao cabinet minister quits Congress party.
newsitem.headline: Former Rao cabinet minister quits Congress party.

text.p: India's Congress party, weighed down by corruption scandals and infighting, suffered a further setback on Saturday when a leading figure resigned to form his own regional grouping, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
Former Food Minister Ajit Singh, who was in the government of ex-Prime Minister Narasimha Rao ousted in elections in May, also quit his seat in the lower house of parliament.
PTI said Singh was launching a new regional party to fight local elections in northern Uttar Pradesh state as an ally of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's ruling United Front coalition.
He blamed Rao for the Congress party's electoral rout.
"As the president of such a big party, Mr Rao should have shown some kind of gesture to resign from the post, accepting its debacle at the elections," PTI quoted Singh as saying.
Rao led the party that has ruled India for all but four years since independence in 1947 to its worst general election defeat this year, but stayed on as party president.
The 74-year-old politician came under pressure from some party colleagues in June after he was issued with a court summons to testify against allegations of corruption.
Indian expatriate Lakhubhai Pathak accused him of paying $100,000 to a Hindu holy man in a failed attempt to secure a government contract.
Rao has also been in the public eye in connection with a fertiliser import scandal, in which one of his sons has been investigated by federal investigators.
Early this year, seven ministers in Rao's cabinet resigned in a bribes-for-favour scandal. They have all been charged.
